test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 8 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following monuments is NOT located in the state of Madhya Pradesh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Janjira Fort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Janjira Fort, also known as Murud-Janjira, is located in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, not in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• This fort is situated on an island off the coastal village of Murud, hence the name Murud-Janjira.
 
• The fort is renowned for being one of the strongest marine forts of India, having withstood several attacks over the centuries.
 
• The fort has a unique architecture with high walls and bastions, and it was originally built by the Siddis, a Muslim dynasty of Indian origin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhandhavgarh Fort**

 
 
• Located in the Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh, Bhandhavgarh Fort is situated within the Bhandhavgarh National Park.
 
• It is one of the oldest forts in India, believed to be over 2,000 years old.
 
• The fort offers panoramic views of the surrounding national park and is historically significant for its association with various dynasties that ruled the region.
 
 
 
• **Gwalior Fort**
 
 
• Gwalior Fort is situated in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh and is considered one of the most impenetrable fortresses in India.
 
• The fort has a rich history and features several palaces, temples, and water tanks within its premises.
 
• It is known for its stunning architecture and has been a part of various historical events in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Asirgarh Fort**
 
 
• Located in the Burhanpur district of Madhya Pradesh, Asirgarh Fort is often referred to as the "key to the Deccan" due to its strategic position.
 
• The fort is perched on a hill and offers a commanding view of the surrounding region, making it a vital military outpost historically.
 
• The fort has three main parts: Asirgarh, Karmargarh, and Malaygarh, each with its own distinct features.
